timelineEvents.title: Gwiazdy Warszawy premieres at Morskie Oko
timelineEvents.label: 30 January 1930 · Gwiazdy Warszawy at Morskie Oko
timelineEvents.shortDescription: The revue Gwiazdy Warszawy opens at the Morskie Oko theatre in Warsaw with Kaper's foxtrot “O tem wróble świergocą”, to words by Andrzej Włast.
timelineEvents.longDescription: While Kaper was living in Berlin, his song reached the Warsaw stage: the revue Gwiazdy Warszawy opened at Morskie Oko on 30 January 1930, announced in Kurjer Warszawski four days earlier. The printed edition names the number as the popular refrain from Morskie Oko in that revue — “Popularny refren z „Morskiego Oka” w rewji „Gwiazdy Warszawy”” — with words by Andrzej Włast and music by Bronisław Kaper, published by Gebethner i Wolff. On 1 February Tygodnik Ilustrowany advertised five dance numbers from the revue, this among them, and Tadeusz Faliszewski recorded it for Syrena-Electro in March. Neither the announcement nor the sheet names the rest of the programme.

places.displayName: Teatr Morskie Oko, Jasna 3 / Sienkiewicza 7, Warsaw
places.publicNote: Warsaw revue theatre that opened in 1928 as a successor to Perskie Oko; Kaper’s “O tem wróble świergocą,” to words by Andrzej Włast, was sung in its revue Gwiazdy Warszawy. Morskie Oko occupied the corner of Jasna 3 and Sienkiewicza 7 from 1928 to 1933; that historical venue address is used for the map.
